From neighborhoods in New York to Abu Dhabi, Uber is igniting opportunities by setting the world in motion. The new café experiences at Uber’s Mission Bay Campus represent a major shift in how Uber employees will eat. With exciting new concepts, made-to-order options, and more space for socializing, meals will become more personalized for each employee, and reflect the unique culture of the Uber community.

Inspired by Uber’s mission and global reach, we’ve developed food concepts that reflect the distinctive flavors and character of neighborhoods across the U.S. that we think will excite Uber’s Mission Bay employees every day. The “neighborhoods” concept can be expanded into Uber’s U.S., Canada, and other global offices. In each place, Bon Appétit will customize the neighborhood experiences to speak to the culture and tastes of employees in each region.

Stations:

Nolita NYC- this New York neighborhood, the home of the famous feast of San Gennaro as featured in “the godfather: part ii,” has a long connection to Italian culture and food. Nolita NYC features a stone hearth oven that offers fresh pizza as well as other oven-fired Italian delicacies like lasagna and baked gnocchi.

The Crescent- this concept is inspired by the diverse flavors of the Mediterranean crescent, which includes France, Spain, Italy, and Greece, as well as countries to the south of the Mediterranean sea such as Libya, Israel, and Tunisia. This culturally rich and fertile area of the world inspires wildly flavorful and healthful dishes.

Deep Ellum- this lively and vibrant area of Dallas is known for its colorful street murals and music scene as much as its grilling and barbecue culture. Uber’s Deep Ellum concept offers grilled items and mouth-watering barbecue from across the spectrum of styles and cultural influences.

Central Valley- our salute to California's central valley, one of the most productive agricultural regions in the world. This concept focuses on plant-forward dishes that celebrate vibrant seasonal vegetables and reflects our enviable proximity to this area and its bounty.

Little Village- known as the “Mexico of the midwest,” this neighborhood of Chicago has a large Latinx population which is reflected in the food and culture. Each year, a large Mexican independence day parade attracts thousands to the neighborhood who come to show pride in their heritage. This station offers Latinx-inspired dishes from Mexico, California.

Food Allergen Warning

Ingredient and allergen information is provided for informational purposes in response to guest requests. Products may change without our knowledge and menu items are prepared in close proximity to other ingredients that may introduce cross-contact with ingredients and/or allergens not listed. We cannot assure against these contingencies. Guests with food allergies or specific dietary concerns should speak with a manager for individualized assistance.

Menu Icon Legend

Peanut: May contain peanuts. All menu items are prepared in an open kitchen that handles all major allergens.
Tree Nuts: May contain tree nuts. All menu items are prepared in an open kitchen that handles all major allergens.
Sesame: May contain sesame. All menu items are prepared in open kitchens that handle all major allergens.
Fish: May contain fish. All menu items are prepared in an open kitchen that handles all major allergens.
Shellfish: May contain shellfish. All menu items are prepared in an open kitchen that handles all major allergens.
Wheat/Gluten: May contain wheat/gluten. Our kitchens are not certified gluten-free so risk of cross-contact is present.
Egg: May contain egg. All menu items are prepared in an open kitchen that handles all major allergens.
Milk: May contain milk. All menu items are prepared in an open kitchen that handles all major allergens.
Soy: May contain soy. All menu items are prepared in an open kitchen that handles all major allergens.

We Are Food Recovery Verified

Your cafés at Uber are Food Recovery Verified! As part of this program we regularly donate wholesome, excess food to a variety of food donation programs. We take leftover food from our café that would otherwise go to waste, and pay it forward within our community.

Just another reason eating with us is good for the community and  the environment!

Learn more at: www.bamco.com/waste

Eat Right — For You

Wellness

When it comes to wellness, Bon Appétit’s focus is on simple, delicious food — that happens to be good for you. To support long-term health, we are bringing more plants to menus every day in a craveable way, while emphasizing healthy cooking techniques. When healthy food tastes good, nourishing your body and mind becomes the easy choice.

Our wellness commitments

Food Allergies

We serve thousands of guests with food allergies and sensitivities safely in our cafés every day. Our chefs, managers, and dietitians work closely with our food-allergic guests to create reasonable solutions to help them eat what they love. If you have questions about eating for your dietary needs in our cafés, reach out to us: we’ll gladly meet with you.

Food allergies & sensitivities

Sustainability

Wellness also includes the health of the animals, the workers, the community, and the Earth. They’re all connected. Bon Appétit has been committed to “food service for a sustainable future” for decades, and we’ve led the food service industry in tackling many important issues, such as cage-free eggs, antibiotics in animal production, and farmworker rights.

Our sustainability commitments
